search_log.method: Inspected the Unicode Roman critical text, selecting individually named persons and recording explicit parentage, marriage, sibling relations, and encounters. Roster-only names are recorded as attendees in 1.177; no kinship inferred from adjacent names.

notes: The largest roster comes from Dhṛṣṭadyumna’s individual enumeration of rulers at Draupadī’s svayaṃvara (1.177.1–20). Generic “others” and unnamed groups are omitted.

Repeated or similar names within the roster are kept as separate source-local nodes where their referents cannot be securely equated (including the two Bṛhadbala entries and multiple Suvarcā/Suvarcas forms).

A few stable figures are reused from earlier Ādiparvan batches via their existing IDs. A source-local unnamed Gandhāra king node is used only for the explicit “sons of the Gandhāra king” relation; no historical identity is inferred.
Mandapāla’s four sons are unnamed in ch. 220 and are not represented; their names occur in later chapter(s), outside the requested 1.220 limit.
One erroneous combined placeholder (“Sundopasunda”) is not emitted; Sunda and Upasunda are separately named and treated as distinct people.
Homonyms shared with earlier lists (for example Bṛhadbala, Suvarcā/Suvarcas, and Uśīnara) are kept branch-scoped unless the passage itself establishes continuity.
The patronymic Auśīnara (1.177.15) is represented as an explicit father relation to Śibi, but its Uśīnara referent is kept separate from the separately listed attendee named Uśīnara in 1.177.18.
The Virocana named among the Kaurava attendees (1.177.2) and Aśvasena, Takṣaka’s son in the Khāṇḍava episode, are branch-scoped to avoid merging same-name entries from other rosters.
